newsitem.title: USA: TEXTRON PLANT TO RESUME OUTPUT AFTER FIRE.
newsitem.headline: TEXTRON PLANT TO RESUME OUTPUT AFTER FIRE.

text.p: Textron Automotive Co. said it expects to resume limited production at its fire-damaged automotive trim plant in Westland, Mich., during the second shift Thursday.
In a prepared statement, the Textron Inc said none of the plant's 400 employees were hurt in the fire on Wednesday night.
Fire damage was contained in the plant's warehouse area, but the remainder of the plant experienced some smoke and water damage.
The plant produces interior headliners for a variety of cars and trucks built by General Motors Corp., Ford Motor Co, Chrysler Corp. and Isuzu Motors Ltd.

GM spokesman Thomas Klipstine said the automaker was initially worried that the fire would disrupt production of its full-size pickup trucks and sport/utilities, which use headliners made at the Textron plant, but later assessments of damage and inventories revealed that production should continue uninterrupted.
"We do not anticipate having to shut down any production lines," Klipstine said.
The Westland Fire Department declared the facility safe for re-entry at 6:30 a.m. EDT, and Textron said employees are leading a major clean-up effort "to minimize interruption to our customers."
